entries.title: PostgreSQL health check probes the wrong port
entries.root_cause: The PostgreSQL service health command probes port 5544 although the server listens on 5432. Change the health check to use the server port.

entries.title: PostgreSQL health check probes the wrong address
entries.root_cause: The PostgreSQL service health command connects to 127.0.0.2 while the server only listens on 127.0.0.1. Change the health check host to the listening address.
entries.differs_from_earlier: Like e1, PostgreSQL never becomes healthy, but the host address is wrong rather than the port.

entries.title: MySQL health check probes the wrong port
entries.root_cause: The MySQL service health command probes port 3307 while mysqld listens on 3306. Change the MySQL health check to use port 3306.
entries.differs_from_earlier: Like e1, a database container fails its readiness check, but this is the MySQL service and its own port setting.

entries.title: PostgreSQL health check probes the wrong port
entries.root_cause: The PostgreSQL service health command probes port 5544 although the server listens on 5432. Change the health check to use the server port.
entries.differs_from_earlier: A later run uses a different runner, container and retry schedule; PostgreSQL still listens on 5432 while the health check uses 5544.
